- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.11 to +0.17).  
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment (e.g., -0.28 or -0.61) — model tends to ignore downward momentum.  
- Overshoot downward after recent highs — model reacts too quickly to price drops, missing mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model overconfidently forecasts higher prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 day horizon.  
- If sentiment turns negative within 3 days, model fails to adjust downward — apply a 1–3% downward correction to next 5-day forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window — apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 7–10 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out — use sentiment-weighted smoothing to avoid overfitting to recent highs.
